name: What should I do first if I’m thinking about a room addition?

mainEntity.name: What should I do first if I’m thinking about a room addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start with a feasibility check: confirm what you want the new space to do, then compare that goal against your lot size, setbacks, height limits, and existing structure. In Denver and nearby cities, a room addition can be blocked or redesigned if zoning, drainage, or structural conditions are not resolved early. A clear first plan saves time, keeps design changes down, and helps you avoid paying for drawings you can’t build. Key items to gather include photos, rough dimensions, survey documents, and a target budget. If you are unsure whether an addition is realistic, a design-build contractor can usually flag the biggest issues before full plans are created.
acceptedAnswer.description: Start by defining the room’s purpose, then check your lot, setbacks, and structure before paying for full plans. That early feasibility step helps avoid redesigns and permit problems later.
